item.title: 🇺🇳 From September 7 to October 7, Geneva will host the 63rd Session of the UN Human Rights Council
item.description: 🇺🇳 From September 7 to October 7, Geneva will host the 63rd Session of the UN Human Rights Council . The Session is expected to address a broad range of issues on the international human rights agenda, including: • protection and promotion of economic, social and cultural rights, • ensuring the right to development, • protection of children, • combating discrimination against women, • advancing the interests of indigenous peoples, • preventing the negative impact of unilateral coercive measures on the enjoyment of human rights, as well as other thematic issues. At Russia’s initiative, a high-level thematic discussion will be held to mark the 60th anniversary of the adoption of the International Covenants on Human Rights . 🇺🇳
From September 7 to October 7, Geneva will host
the 63rd Session of the UN Human Rights Council
.
The Session
is expected to address
a broad range of issues
on the international human rights agenda, including:
• protection and promotion of economic, social and cultural rights,
• ensuring the right to development,
• protection of children,
• combating discrimination against women,
• advancing the interests of indigenous peoples,
• preventing the negative impact of unilateral coercive measures on the enjoyment of human rights, as well as other thematic issues.
At Russia’s initiative, a high-level thematic discussion will be held to mark the
60th anniversary of the adoption of the International Covenants on Human Rights
.
The Council will adopt
the outcomes of the Universal Periodic Review of the national reports
of Belgium, Denmark, Latvia, Namibia, Niger, Nicaragua, Mozambique, Palau, Paraguay, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Singapore, Somalia, Sierra Leone and Estonia.
At the initiative of the EU, the Council will once again consider
a
politicised and highly confrontational
draft resolution
on the human rights situation in Russia, aimed at extending for another year the mandate of the relevant HRC Special Rapporteur,
Mariana Katzarova
of Bulgaria.
❗️
Russia’s stance on this matter
remains unchanged
: we do not recognise the mandate of this illegitimate special procedure, and any form of interaction with it is unacceptable to us.
The Russian delegation, which will participate in the Session
as an observer
, intends, as before, to make active use of all available opportunities
to overcome confrontation
and
promote a unifying agenda
, as well as
to foster among international partners an understanding of the importance of establishing constructive international dialogue
on the promotion and protection of human rights, with due respect for the national, religious, cultural and historical characteristics of every state.
A number of special side events
will be organised to present Russia’s approaches to the most pressing issues on the session’s agenda to the international community.

#AmbassadorSpeaks
✍️
Comment by Ambassador of the Russian Federation to South Africa Roman Ambаrov on the 20th Anniversary of the Treaty of Friendship and Partnership between Russia and South Africa
On 5-6 September 2006,
Russian President Vladimir Putin
paid the first-ever visit to the Republic of South Africa
.
This landmark event marked a turning point in the development of Russian-South African relations and gave fresh impetus to their consistent strengthening.
🇷🇺
🇿🇦
The signing of the
Treaty of Friendship and Partnership
in Cape Town laid a solid legal foundation for long-term cooperation.
Moscow and Pretoria
demonstrated their shared commitment to systematic and strategic cooperation
, based on common approaches to key international issues, mutual respect for national interests and the principles of the sovereign equality of states.
🤝
Over the past two decades, our countries have progressed from political rapprochement to a
comprehensive, strategic and multifaceted partnership
encompassing energy, mining, science, space and human capital development. Trade and economic ties, interregional cooperation, as well as humanitarian and cultural exchanges occupy an important place on the bilateral agenda.
A significant role in advancing these areas is played by established
intergovernmental and interagency mechanisms
, including the Joint Intergovernmental Committee on Trade and Economic Cooperation, the Russia-South Africa Business Council, and joint commissions on scientific and military-technical cooperation.
A key milestone in advancing a constructive agenda in world affairs was the adoption in
2013 of the Joint Declaration on the Establishment of a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership
, which elevated relations between our countries to a new level. The document reaffirmed the parties’ commitment to developing cooperation “in the political, economic, trade, scientific, technological, cultural and other fields”, creating a foundation for further expansion of practical cooperation.
Regular contacts at the highest and senior levels continue to
demonstrate the strong momentum
of the bilateral agenda.
🌍
Of particular importance are the joint efforts of Russia and South Africa on the international fora, primarily the
#UN
,
#BRICS
and the
#G20
, where our countries advocate strengthening multilateralism and building a more just system of international relations.
People-to-people ties remain an integral part of our mutually beneficial partnership.
We are interested in further expanding educational opportunities for South African students in Russia, developing academic exchanges and strengthening cultural ties. Creative and educational initiatives contribute not only to expanding practical cooperation, but also to fostering a deeper mutual understanding between our peoples.
This anniversary is not merely an occasion to look back. It is also a point of reference for the future.
We see considerable potential for deepening cooperation in high technologies and digitalisation, as well as for further developing energy, scientific and technological and investment cooperation.
An important priority is also the expansion of direct contacts between Russia’s regions and South Africa’s provinces, creating additional opportunities for implementing joint projects.
As a more just and multipolar world order takes shape,
Russia and South Africa, united by their shared commitment to the principles of the sovereign equality of states,
can set an example of mature, responsible and mutually beneficial dialogue.
☝️
We are convinced that the spirit of the Cape Town agreements of 2006 remains a reliable compass for the continued advancement of our countries towards one another — in the interests of the well-being and prosperity of our peoples, as well as ensuring security and stability both on the African continent and on the international stage.
#RussiaSouthAfrica
#AmbassadorAmbarov

item.title: ✍️ Article by Ambassador of Russia to Indonesia Sergei Tolchenov titled « The Final Days of World War II: The Defeat and Surrender of Japan»
item.description: ✍️ Article by Ambassador of Russia to Indonesia Sergei Tolchenov titled « The Final Days of World War II: The Defeat and Surrender of Japan» published in Jakarta Globe (04.09.2026) Key points: • September 3 marks the Day of Military Glory in Russia, known as the "Day of Victory over Militarist Japan and the End of World War II" . The defeat of Japanese militarism eliminated the last major stronghold of the Axis powers in the Asia-Pacific region , as well as Nazi Germany’s ally in the Far East, which had occupied vast territories and subjugated numerous peoples. • Japan’s war in Asia and the Pacific claimed the lives of an estimated 36 million people and caused immense destruction and suffering. In China alone, 10–15 million people were massacred. On the island of Java, 3–4 million were killed , while in Indochina the death toll reached 1–1.5 million. Japan lost 2.1 million military personnel and 800,000 civilians. Some 36,000 Soviet officers and soldiers lost their lives during the liberation of China and Korea from Japanese occupation. • On August 9, 1945, the Soviet Union, f ulfilling the commitments it had undertaken at the Yalta Conference of the Allied powers (February 4–11, 1945), entered the war against Japan. The Red Army launched a rapid advance deep into Manchuria. By August 20, after fierce fighting, Soviet forces had reached the Manchurian Plain, split Japanese forces into separate groupings and encircled them. Japanese troops began surrendering in large numbers.

Article
by Ambassador of Russia to Indonesia
Sergei Tolchenov
titled «
The Final Days of World War II: The Defeat and Surrender of Japan»
published in
Jakarta Globe
(04.09.2026)
Key points:
• September 3 marks the Day of Military Glory in Russia, known as the
"Day of Victory over Militarist Japan and the End of World War II"
. The defeat of Japanese militarism
eliminated the last major stronghold of the Axis powers in the Asia-Pacific region
, as well as Nazi Germany’s ally in the Far East, which had occupied vast territories and subjugated numerous peoples.
• Japan’s war in Asia and the Pacific claimed the lives of an
estimated 36 million people
and caused immense destruction and suffering. In China alone, 10–15 million people were massacred. On the island of Java,
3–4 million were killed
, while in Indochina the death toll reached 1–1.5 million. Japan lost 2.1 million military personnel and 800,000 civilians. Some 36,000 Soviet officers and soldiers lost their lives during the liberation of China and Korea from Japanese occupation.
• On August 9, 1945, the Soviet Union, f
ulfilling the commitments it had undertaken
at the Yalta Conference of the Allied powers (February 4–11, 1945), entered the war against Japan. The Red Army launched a rapid advance deep into Manchuria. By August 20, after fierce fighting, Soviet forces had reached the Manchurian Plain, split Japanese forces into separate groupings and encircled them.
Japanese troops began surrendering in large numbers.
• On September 2, 1945, aboard the American battleship USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay, with representatives of the Allied powers in attendance, the Instrument of Surrender of Japan was signed, bringing to
a formal end the largest conflict in human history
, unleashed by fascism and Hitlerism in alliance with Japanese militarism.
• The memory of the horrors of World War II and its consequences
remains deeply important today
. Developments around the world show how easily some countries’ leaders, influenced by Nazi and militarist ideas and pursuing revanchist policies,
can forget the tragic chapters of their own history and their past crimes
, especially when acknowledging them runs counter to their current political interests.

item.title: 🗓 Today is Lake Baikal Day . It is celebrated in Russia in late August, early September.
item.description: 🗓 Today is Lake Baikal Day . It is celebrated in Russia in late August, early September. There is no single date, however, as the lake is located across several regions of the Russian Federation — Irkutsk Region, the Republic of Buryatia and Zabaykalsky Krai — each of which sets its own date for the celebration. Thus, in Buryatia , Lake Baikal Day is observed on the first Sunday of August; in Irkutsk Region — on the first Sunday of September; and in Zabaykalsky Krai — on the second Sunday of September. The different dates make it possible to hold environmental, educational and cultural events over several weeks, ensuring maximum public attention to Lake Baikal and the need to preserve its unique ecosystem. The date was first established in 1999 at the initiative of public organisations and environmentalists. The immediate impetus was # Baikal ’s inclusion in 1996 on the #UNESCO World Heritage List. The decision was based on the unique combination of geological features significant for the study of the Earth’s evolution, as well as the richness and diversity of Baikal’s flora and fauna. 🗓
Today is
Lake Baikal Day
. It is celebrated in Russia in late August, early September.
There is no single date, however, as
the lake is located across several regions of the Russian Federation
— Irkutsk Region, the Republic of Buryatia and Zabaykalsky Krai — each of which sets its own date for the celebration.
Thus,
in Buryatia
, Lake Baikal Day is observed on the first Sunday of August;
in Irkutsk Region
— on the first Sunday of September; and
in Zabaykalsky Krai
— on the second Sunday of September. The different dates make it possible to hold environmental, educational and cultural events over several weeks, ensuring
maximum public attention to Lake Baikal
and the need to preserve its unique ecosystem.
The date was first established in 1999 at the initiative of public organisations and environmentalists. The immediate impetus was
#
Baikal
’s inclusion in 1996 on the
#UNESCO
World Heritage List.
The decision was based on the unique combination of geological features significant for the study of the Earth’s evolution, as well as the richness and diversity of Baikal’s flora and fauna. The lake’s inclusion on the UNESCO list confirmed its
global environmental value
.
💬
From the
greeting
by
Alexander Kozlov
, Minister of Natural Resources and Environment of Russia, on the occasion of Lake Baikal Day:
Preserving Baikal and its ecosystems is
one of the priorities of Russia’s state environmental policy.
To this end, a network of specially protected natural areas has been established, and Russia’s first nature reserve, the Barguzinsky Nature Reserve, was created right here, on the shores of Lake Baikal.
***
🔹
Lake Baikal is 636 km long, stretching from southwest to northeast
in the shape of a giant crescent.
Its width ranges from 24 to 79 km, while its water surface covers
31,722 km²
(excluding islands). The length of its shoreline
exceeds 2,000 km.
Baikal is the deepest lake on the planet.
Its maximum depth reaches
1,642 metres
, while its average depth is approximately 744 metres.
Lake Baikal contains approximately
23,615 km³ of water.
It is the world’s largest natural reservoir of fresh water, holding
around 20% of the world’s surface freshwater reserves.
Baikal is a true museum of endemic species — species found nowhere else on Earth. The lake is home to
around 2,600 species of animals and plants
, approximately 60–70% of which are endemic, including the beloved Baikal seal —
the world’s only freshwater seal species.
#Russia

Vladimir Putin:
Colleagues, I heartily welcome you to Moscow.
The situation we are to sort out today is, of course, a difficult one.
But before we begin, I would like to ask you to convey my
best wishes and words of gratitude
to the President of the United States,
Donald Trump.
While he realizes that he is facing a difficult situation,
he nevertheless does not stop his efforts to resolve
it and to contribute to the settlement of the
Russian‑Ukrainian conflict.
Today, we will discuss all its components and all its aspects, and for our part, we are also ready to inform you about our view of the situation.
As you informed us, I know that you are planning to go to Kiev after visiting Moscow. In any case, of course, no matter what happens next,
contacts of this kind are certainly always beneficial.
And here, of course, the quality of mediation and trust in those who are engaged in it are very important. I’d like to tell you that
we find it comfortable to work with you,
and, of course, we have a very high level of trust during this work.
🤝
We are glad to see you. Welcome.
***
We received the request through official channels — both through the intelligence services and through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs — to stop the strikes on Kiev.
I issued the respective order,
and since midnight on September 5, these
strikes on Kiev have not been carried out.
I would like to note that the Ukrainian side has also significantly reduced — by an order of magnitude — the strikes on the territory of the Russian Federation, including Moscow.
The Ukrainian authorities have published their call for a broader three‑day truce, but we have never agreed on this with them.
Yet we will do everything in our power to ensure the
safety of the negotiation process
and the mediators, represented by you and, perhaps, by those accompanying you.
#RussiaUS

item.title: 💬 Vladimir Medinsky Aide to the President of Russia and Chairman of the Russian Military Historical Society:
item.description: 💬 Vladimir Medinsky , Aide to the President of Russia and Chairman of the Russian Military Historical Society: 🌟 On September 4 in Khabarovsk, on the high bank of the Amur River, the Russian Military Historical Society and Khabarovsk Region Governor Dmitry Demeshin unveiled Russia’s largest memorial dedicated to the Victory over militarist Japan and the end of World War II . A 15-meter high bronze Soviet soldier is the centrepiece of the composition . With the stock of his rifle, he smashes a border post bearing a chrysanthemum – not only the emblem of Japan’s Imperial House, but also a symbol of the militarism responsible for monstrous crimes . In August-September 1945, Marshal Alexander Vassilevsky commanded Soviet forces from Khabarovsk. In just three weeks, they defeated Japan’s million-strong Kwantung Army and brought World War II to an end . PS. In terms of the ratio between duration, losses and results, the operation to defeat the Japanese army in the Far East was the most effective military operation in history. #Victory81
